synopsis: The corpus concludes that no single method can deliver valid camera, radar, lidar and ultrasonic environments across 100+ site types in the available time; it recommends parameterized representative sites, procedural rules and asset libraries anchored to surveyed real sites [f75, f76, f3705]. A proposed starting point is 15–30 site archetypes anchored by 3–5 surveyed sites, explicitly planning assumptions rather than evidence; no published method or standard setting the required number was found [f11937, f255]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, abstract closed-loop machine and site simulation is considered realistic by mid-2027, with sensor-independent geometry, scenario and evaluation foundations recommended now [f844, f1592]. Photorealism alone does not establish sensor validity: separate sensor and physical layers need material data, cross-sensor geometry and timing must remain consistent, and sensor/environment fidelity remains the hardest uncertainty [f85, f86, f5101, f10424]. Road-oriented formats fit lane-free sites poorly; custom off-road representations are often needed, while OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0.0, dated April 2025, standardizes assets and material properties for sensor-perception simulation [f7157, f8724, f7083]. Building meaningful site/material assets took more effort than rendering in the one heavy-machine study found, and published environment-building effort, cost, team-size or timeline figures were not found [f4457, f256].
